neighbours.label: the ending after 'mach' in macho / machismo (and the similar 'Cam-acho'), Spanish-origin word pieces
fire: He refused to see a doctor because he thought it was too macho to complain.
The film pokes fun at the machismo of small-town cowboys.
Critics say the coach's macho attitude hurts his young players.
She wrote an essay on machismo in Latin American politics.
The wine has a bold, almost macho strength on the palate.
Divers found a male spider crab, a macho, at thirteen metres.
His macho posturing in the debate did not impress the voters.
The novel's hero slowly lets go of the machismo he grew up with.
quiet: He refused to see a doctor because he thought it was too weak to complain.
The film pokes fun at the pride of small-town cowboys.
Critics say the coach's harsh attitude hurts his young players.
She wrote an essay on populism in Latin American politics.
The wine has a bold, almost smoky strength on the palate.
Divers found a large spider crab, a female, at thirteen metres.
His loud posturing in the debate did not impress the voters.
The novel's hero slowly lets go of the anger he grew up with.

notes: the + pole is the piece 'Camb' (Cambodia, Cambrian)
